messages.author: a992ec8c745f6a5e
messages.subject: Trouble installing cmdstan 2.9.0 in Windows 10
parts:
Hi all,

I've been struggling with the build step of installation of cmdstan 2.9.0.  I'm using the Rtools utilities (and both make and g++ seem to be working fine, as best I can tell...).  Here's the output from "make build". There are a lot of undefined references to stan::lang, but I'm not sure if that's the ultimate problem. The final line before exiting is "collect2: ld returned 1 exit status".     

Has anyone else had this problem, and does anyone have any suggestions?

Much thanks,

Dan



P.S. Just in case it comes up, yes I have 4 cores, and the result does not change whether of not I use the -j4 flag.

messages.author: a992ec8c745f6a5e
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Trouble installing cmdstan 2.9.0 in Windows 10
parts:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for the response.  I used the zip from here, but I think I found my problem -- among the warnings and errors was a "FIND: Parameter format not correct" (I've been basically pasting every line of the output into google one at a time, looking for clues), and I found this thread in which someone had the Rtools utilities on their path, but the windows find.exe from Windows\system32 was earlier (this is normal as the system path is typically pre-pended to the user path as far as I can tell).  My solution was to remove the Rtools directories from my user path and add them to the system path, but earlier than the Windows\system32 entry (in my case, by right-clicking the windows menu > System > Advanced System Settings > Environment Variables, and then editing the user and system variables.  I think if you don't have admin rights, you might be out of luck though, since the system path's Windows\system32\find.exe will always supersede  the user's path's Rtools\bin\find.exe.  This might be worth a mention in Appendix B.3 in the cmdstan guide.

Thanks,
Dan
